security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, biological taxonomy IDs, or documented ETE cache behavior. The confirmed issue is privileged system package installation guidance using sudo apt-get in SKILL.md. No prompt-injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo examples with a clear warning that privileged package installation requires explicit user approval and trusted package sources.
Document the cache path, approximate download size, and options for using a custom database file near NCBITaxa examples.
Label command blocks as optional manual steps so agents do not treat setup commands as automatic actions.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic tree work often needs repeatable manipulation, taxonomy lookup, and figure generation. This skill provides ETE patterns, helper scripts, and workflows for bioinformatics analysis.
actual_capabilities: Load, write, prune, reroot, and compare phylogenetic trees in common ETE-supported formats.
Detect evolutionary events and identify orthologs or paralogs with PhyloTree workflows.
Translate species names and taxonomic IDs with NCBITaxa examples.
Render trees as PDF, SVG, or PNG with layouts, node styles, labels, and faces.
Use helper scripts for tree statistics, format conversion, pruning, rerooting, and quick visualization.
Work with clustering dendrograms and data matrices through ClusterTree examples.
limitations: Requires Python and the ete3 package in the user environment.
GUI rendering can require Qt or operating system packages.
NCBITaxa may download a large taxonomy database on first use.
Does not validate biological assumptions or input data quality.

use_cases.title: Prepare Gene Tree Analyses
use_cases.description: Build repeatable workflows for loading gene trees, detecting duplications, and exporting ortholog groups.

use_cases.title: Annotate Species Trees
use_cases.description: Map species names to taxonomic IDs and add lineage data to tree leaves.

use_cases.title: Create Publication Figures
use_cases.description: Design styled tree diagrams with support labels, clade colors, and vector output formats.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Tree Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the safest ETE workflow to load a Newick tree, count leaves, midpoint root it, and save a copy.

prompt_templates.title: Prune and Compare Trees
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an ETE workflow to prune two trees to shared taxa, preserve branch lengths, and compare Robinson-Foulds distance.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate with Taxonomy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ETE approach to map leaf species names to NCBI taxids and add lineage features before visualization.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Phylogenomics Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a full PhyloTree workflow for event detection, ortholog extraction, taxonomy annotation, and publication figure export.

output_examples.input: User asks for a simple tree preprocessing plan.
output: Load the input tree with the correct Newick format.
Create a copy before pruning or rerooting.
Midpoint root the copy and preserve branch lengths during pruning.
Save the result under a new output filename.

output_examples.input: User asks how to annotate leaves with taxonomy.
output: Extract species names from leaf labels.
Resolve names to taxonomic IDs with NCBITaxa.
Store taxid and lineage features on each matching leaf.
Report missing or ambiguous species names for review.

output_examples.input: User asks for publication figure guidance.
output: Use PDF or SVG for editable vector output.
Apply node styles based on support values or clade membership.
Hide default leaf labels when custom aligned labels are used.
Test layout on a subset before rendering a large tree.

best_practices: Work on copied trees before pruning, rerooting, or resolving polytomies.
Confirm taxonomy cache size and location before using NCBITaxa in a new environment.
Use vector formats for publication figures and raster formats for quick previews.
anti_patterns: Running privileged package installation commands without explicit user approval.
Assuming all leaf names map cleanly to species or NCBI taxonomic IDs.
Opening very large trees interactively before testing rendering settings on a subset.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps use ETE Toolkit for tree manipulation, taxonomy annotation, phylogenetic analysis, and visualization.

faq.question: Does it install ETE automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance and examples, but the user controls any package installation.

faq.question: Which tree formats are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover Newick, NHX, PhyloXML, NeXML, and ETE Newick format options.

faq.question: Can it create publication figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents ETE rendering to PDF, SVG, and PNG with styling and layout options.

faq.question: Does NCBITaxa require network access?
faq.answer: First use can download a large local NCBI taxonomy database unless a database file already exists.

faq.question: Is biological validation included?
faq.answer: No. Users must validate sequence quality, taxon naming, and phylogenetic assumptions independently.
